rationale: The workflow repeatedly installs dependencies (distro packages via apt/dnf/pacman custom actions plus Perl modules via cpanm) on every matrix cell with no cache, so dependency caching is the closest candidate (pattern P-LIT-GHA-CACHE; measured example experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2). However, it does not fit this repository: the only concrete measured cache example is Python/pip keyed on hashFiles('pyproject.toml'), while this is a Perl (Monitorix) multi-distro container workflow with no pyproject.toml, no Perl lockfile/cpanfile, and no verified persistent, portable cache directory across the archlinux/almalinux/rockylinux/debian/fedora/ubuntu matrix. Pattern P-LIT-GHA-CACHE's precondition that cache inputs include a lockfile plus environment is not satisfied by the provided files (only env dependency lists and a Makefile). Other candidates are not supported: each matrix distro result is a required compatibility check, so canceling remaining jobs on failure (P-LIT-FAIL-FAST) would lose required diagnostics, and there is no representative per-job duration history justifying a job-level timeout (P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT). Adding a speculative cache would be an unrelated/no-op change and could weaken coverage, so no supported optimization is applied.
